summary: Adds user search, per-key request counting and an upstream status endpoint to the directory API, and registers them in main.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.problem: Search formats the name query parameter directly into the SQL text with Sprintf. A quote in name escapes the string literal.
findings.consequence: Any client calling GET /users can read or change arbitrary database rows.
findings.fix: Use a placeholder in the query and pass name to QueryContext as a bound argument.
findings.suggested_change: rows, err := h.DB.QueryContext(r.Context(), "SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE name = ?", name)

findings.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
findings.problem: Count locks h.mu and then returns early when key is empty without unlocking. The mutex stays held forever.
findings.consequence: One request to GET /count without a key blocks every later Count request permanently.
findings.fix: Check key before taking the lock, or defer h.mu.Unlock() right after locking.

findings.title: Response body closed before error check
findings.problem: fetchStatus defers resp.Body.Close() before checking err. When http.Get fails, resp is nil and the deferred call dereferences it.
findings.consequence: An unreachable upstream makes GET /upstream panic instead of returning 502.
findings.fix: Move the defer after the err check.

findings.title: New handlers have no tests
findings.problem: The change adds Search, Count and Upstream handlers. No test file in the repository exercises them.
findings.consequence: Regressions such as the lock leak and nil dereference go unnoticed until production.
findings.fix: Add httptest based tests covering each handler, including the error paths.

dropped.reason: This hit flags the same Sprintf query that the c1 finding already raises.
